description: A polyphonic oscillator that bends the phase of its wave, with glide, an amplitude control, three modulation inputs, hard sync and a noise output

params.text: Sets the pitch, in semitones either side of middle C; in LFO mode the same knob is read as a power of two instead, reaching far below the audible range
Sets how long the pitch takes to slide from one note to the next; below about a fiftieth of its travel there is no slide at all, and it does nothing in LFO mode
Bends the phase of the wave, 0.02 to 0.98: on the sine and triangle it works towards a sawtooth, and on the square it works like pulse width
Sets how far the voltage at the BM jack moves the bend, from full inversion through nothing at the middle to full
Sets how far the voltage at the FM jack moves the frequency, from full inversion through nothing at the middle to full
Switches LFO mode on and off: the three wave outputs drop far below the audible range and swing 0-10V rather than either side of zero, and glide stops working
Sets the level of the three wave outputs, 0 to 1
Sets how far the voltage at the AM jack moves the level, from full inversion through nothing at the middle to full

inputs.text: Restarts the wave from the beginning whenever the voltage here crosses, which is hard sync; the square output of another oscillator is the usual thing to patch
Sets the pitch, 1V per octave added to the frequency knob, and its channel count is what sets the polyphony of the whole module
Moves the bend away from the knob setting, a fifth per volt scaled by the BM knob, and the total is held between 0.02 and 0.98
Moves the frequency away from the knob setting, scaled by the FM knob; it is added to the frequency itself rather than to the pitch, which is linear frequency modulation
Moves the level away from the knob setting, a fifth per volt scaled by the AM knob, and the total is held between 0 and 1

outputs.text: The square wave, ±5V, or 0-10V in LFO mode; it is drawn from a softened table in oscillator mode and a hard-edged one in LFO mode
The sine wave, ±5V, or 0-10V in LFO mode
The triangle wave, ±5V, or 0-10V in LFO mode
White noise, one channel for each channel of the oscillator

notes: the module is polyphonic and takes its channel count from the pitch input; with nothing patched there it runs one channel
in LFO mode the three wave outputs stop swinging either side of zero and run from 0V upwards instead
the frequency is held below half the sample rate, so heavy frequency modulation stops rather than folding back
menu: Interpolation mode: Linear, None — chooses whether the wavetable is read with interpolation between entries or by taking the nearest entry, which is rougher
Use DD cable color scheme - Light — replaces Rack's cable colour list with five colours of the maker's, after a confirmation step; the item ends in Dark under the Rack dark-panel setting

inputs.1:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V.
